text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would raise its annual main interest rate to 5.70 percent from 5.59 percent, effective Monday.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it extended the deadline for negotiations for the sale of a 57 percent stake in the country's fertiliser producer Chimko to September 12.
-- Around 81 percent of Bulgarians support the opening of secret police files from the communist era under a new law approved last month, Mediana polling agency figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's July unemployment was virtually unchanged from June at 14.2 percent of the workforce, The National Labour Exchange said. @

-- Bulgaria is expected to introduce this autumn a new mechanism for licensing traders in alchohol, cigarettes and fuels under which licences will be issued by the government rather than by municipal authorities, Price Commission chairman Mladen Mladenov said.
-- A bomb had exploded in an appartment block of flats in Bulgaria's western town of Breznik, police said. Nobody was killed by the explosion but 11 people were injured. @

-- The World Bank is expected to approve in September a contract for consultancy services in the sale of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the Privatisation Agency said.

-- An International Monetary Fund technical mission is expected to arrive in Sofia at the beginning of September to discuss the progress of tax reform with the Bulgarian government, Finance minister Muravei Radev said.
-- Bulgaria's police said it had revealed white collar crimes for 61 billion levs for the first six months of this year. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
